sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Hempstead
sections.html:
The Town of Hempstead Receiver of Taxes collects it. The office is on the first floor at 200 N Franklin Street, Hempstead, NY 11550, and counter hours run Monday through Friday from 9 am to 4:45 pm. The phone number is 516-538-1500.

One Hempstead payment reaches many bodies. The Receiver collects for Nassau County, the town, 99 special districts and 33 school districts, then forwards the money to school district treasurers and the other districts at no charge. The Receiver is an independently elected town official, and state law makes that person personally responsible for the money the office takes in and distributes.

The town covers 22 incorporated villages, and one of them is also named Hempstead. The town does not collect for incorporated villages, so a house inside a village may carry a separate village bill. Ask the village hall whether one applies to your parcel.

Hempstead owners receive two bills a year, and each is paid in halves. The General bill, which covers county, town and special districts, goes out in January. The School bill goes out in October. Every half has a penalty-free collection period of 40 days.

  • School tax: first half through November 10, second half through May 10. The Receiver keeps taking school payments through May 31.
  • General tax: first half through February 10, second half through August 10. The Receiver keeps taking general payments through August 31.
  • A 1% discount on the second half applies when both school halves are paid by November 10, or both general halves by February 10. The discounted figure is printed under the total box on the bill.

After a levy closes, payment goes to the Nassau County Treasurer at 1 West Street, Mineola, 516-571-2090. The county runs its own late schedule, so call before you send a check. A bill with the word "arrears" in its upper left corner means unpaid tax is already collecting penalties at the county.

sections.h2: What a late school tax payment costs
sections.html:
A first-half school payment picks up 2% on November 11 and gains another point each month after that, reaching 8% in May. The second half has a single step: 2% from May 11 to May 31. The General levy has its own schedule, so ask the Receiver for it.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Hempstead tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay in person, by mail, online, by phone or at one of several satellite points. Pick the one that gives you a dated receipt before the deadline.

  • The Receiver's office on N Franklin Street, where tax cashiers issue an immediate receipt.
  • The EZ-Pay Drive-Thru window behind the Receiver's office, plus satellite offices at Levittown Hall and Rock Hall Museum and a mobile tax office. These give a temporary receipt, and the final one is mailed within seven business days.
  • Online or by phone with a card or electronic check through the Receiver's Payment Center.
  • Mail, with the number 1 stub for a first half, the number 2 stub for a second half, or both stubs for the full year.

Card payments carry a 2.3% convenience fee with a $1.50 minimum. Visa debit is a flat $3.95, and an e-check costs $0.90. The fees go to the payment processor, eGov Strategies, and not to the town. A mailed payment only counts if it has an official U.S. Postal Service cancellation date on or before the last penalty-free day, because a metered postmark is not accepted. Owners aged 65 or older, or with a disability, who own a one to three family home can name a third party to receive a duplicate bill.

sections.h2: Who sets a Hempstead assessment, and when can I challenge it?
sections.html:
Nassau County sets your assessment, and the town does not. The county's Assessment Review Commission is an agency separate from the Department of Assessment, and it takes appeals online through a system called AROW. The commission sits at 240 Old Country Road, 5th Floor, Mineola, and answers at 516-571-3214.

The next tentative roll is dated January 4, 2027, with grievances due March 1, 2027. The final roll follows on April 3, 2028, and court petitions are due May 1, 2028. That roll feeds the 2028/29 school year and the 2029 town and county bills. Filing a grievance costs nothing and needs no lawyer.

If the commission denies your complaint, a Small Claims Assessment Review is open to owners who live in a one, two or three family home. The state charges a $30 filing fee and gives you a 30 day window after the final roll is filed.

sections.h2: Exemptions that can lower a Hempstead bill
sections.html:
The town lists six programs: senior citizens, military service, disability or limited income, STAR, home improvement, and volunteer firefighters and ambulance personnel. Applications go to the Nassau County Department of Assessment, which accepts them year-round, and the filing deadline is January 2. Call 516-571-1500 for forms.

STAR works differently for new applicants. They register with the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance and receive a credit check, not a bill reduction. The Receiver also runs tax forums around the town on exemptions, challenges and early-payment discounts, and sellers who have never claimed anything may find a missed program worth checking before listing.

sections.h2: What happens to Hempstead property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax stays attached to the parcel until someone pays it, so the sale needs a payoff figure. Settle these items before the closing date:

  • Ask the Receiver at 516-538-1500 which halves of the School and General bills are paid.
  • If a bill shows "arrears," call the Nassau County Treasurer at 516-571-2090 for the amount, since the Receiver no longer holds that tax.
  • Expect exemptions to drop off at transfer. The Department of Assessment removes any exemption a new owner does not qualify for, which is why a buyer's bill can differ a lot from yours.
  • Have the new owner send the ownership and mortgage change form to the Receiver. The town warns owners not to assume an attorney or lender will do it.

A cash purchase can build the tax payoff into the closing statement, so the money never has to come out of your pocket first. If you are behind on Hempstead tax and a lender or lien is involved, get a written payoff from each office first. If you are partway through a bill, a sale in the middle of a penalty period is worth timing, since each month of delay adds another point to the penalty.

Hempstead village is dense and mostly renter-heavy, with 17,108 households at 3.37 people each. Owners occupy 47.5% of homes, the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $459,500, rent runs $1,622 at the median, and household income sits at $90,420. The village covers 3.69 square miles and had an estimated 59,819 residents in July 2025. The wider town is the most populous in New York State, at 793,409 people in the 2020 census.

Houses here sell on their own tax bill and condition, so a fresh payoff letter helps more than a neighborhood average.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Hempstead property tax in person?
faqs.a: At the Receiver of Taxes, 200 N Franklin Street, First Floor, Hempstead, NY 11550. The drive-thru window behind the building and the satellite offices at Levittown Hall and Rock Hall Museum also take payments.

faqs.q: Can I still pay school tax to the Hempstead Receiver after May 31?
faqs.a: No. School tax can be paid to the Receiver through May 31, and general tax through August 31. After that, payment goes to the Nassau County Treasurer at 1 West Street in Mineola, 516-571-2090.

faqs.q: Does the Town of Hempstead set my assessment?
faqs.a: No. Nassau County sets assessments, and appeals go to the county's Assessment Review Commission. The next tentative roll is dated January 4, 2027, and grievances are due March 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Will my exemptions pass to the buyer of my Hempstead house?
faqs.a: No. When title transfers, the Nassau County Department of Assessment removes exemptions the new owner is not entitled to. The buyer's first bill can be much higher than yours.

faqs.q: What does it mean if my Hempstead bill says arrears?
faqs.a: It means unpaid tax is already accruing penalties at the Nassau County Treasurer's office. Contact the Treasurer at 516-571-2090 before you pay anything, because the county uses a different penalty schedule than the town.
